toolsPreview.name: search_eu_textile_regulations
toolsPreview.description:
Search the Reecopedia corpus of EU textile sustainability regulations.

Returns the most relevant regulatory passages with citations (source file,
page, section). Answer the user's question ONLY from these passages and
cite them. Corpus: ESPR 2024/1781, Digital Product Passport, CSRD, CBAM,
EU ETS, CWA 18291, JRC BREF and textile preparatory studies, EP studies.

toolsPreview.name: about_reecopedia
toolsPreview.description: What Reecopedia is, who runs it, and its privacy policy.

toolsPreview.name: report_answer_issue
toolsPreview.description:
Report that an answer built from Reecopedia search results was wrong,
misleading or incomplete. The report (query + reason, nothing else — no
personal data) enters Reecopedia's human curation queue and is reviewed
weekly to correct the corpus and retrieval quality.

Call this when the user flags an answer as wrong, or when you notice the
retrieved passages contradict the answer you gave.

toolsPreview.name: search
toolsPreview.description:
Search EU textile sustainability regulations (ESPR, DPP, CSRD, CBAM,
EU ETS, CWA 18291, JRC studies). Deep-research interface: returns a list
of matching regulatory passages as {results: [{id, title, text, url}]}.
Pass a result `id` to the `fetch` tool to get the full document page.

toolsPreview.name: fetch
toolsPreview.description: Fetch the full text of a regulatory document page returned by `search`.

toolsPreview.name: document_outline
toolsPreview.description:
Return the heading tree (table of sections) of an indexed document,
so you can explore its structure before fetching pages. Each entry has
the heading text, its full path, depth and first page: pass the page to
`fetch` as "<document>#p<page>" to read it.

toolsPreview.name: find_exact_text
toolsPreview.description:
Find literal occurrences of an exact string in the corpus — article
numbers, regulation ids, precise wording (e.g. "Article 8(3)",
"2024/1781"). Complements semantic `search`: use this when you need the
exact string, not the concept. Returns one match per (file, page) with an
occurrence count and a text snippet; read the full page with `fetch`.
Scans the literal chunk text of both indexes the semantic search serves
(the two chunkings differ, so some passages exist in only one); the
synthetic contextual enrichment is NOT scanned — it is not document text.
